title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in Florida's 14th Congressional District
description: The 2026 election for Florida's 14th Congressional District pits longtime Democratic incumbent Kathy Castor against a crowded field of Republican challengers in a newly redrawn district. Governor Ron DeSantis signed a new congressional map in May 2026 that shifted the district from a Democratic-leaning seat (Harris +7% in 2024) to one that favored Donald Trump by roughly 10 percentage points, making it one of the most competitive House races in Florida. Castor, first elected in 2006, is seeking a 12th term while arguing that the redistricting is an unconstitutional partisan gerrymander. The Republican primary features several well-funded candidates, including former state Rep. Mike Beltran and state Rep. Kevin Steele, both of whom have self-funded significant sums, while the general election will test whether Castor's long incumbency and name recognition can overcome the district's new Republican advantage.
polling_note: No publicly available general election polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The primary election is scheduled for August 18, 2026, and most polling to date has focused on the competitive Republican primary rather than the general election matchup.

candidates.name: Kathy Castor
candidates.summary: Kathy Castor is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to a 12th term representing Florida's 14th Congressional District. First elected in 2006, she previously served on the Hillsborough County Commission from 2002 to 2006. Castor was born in Miami, earned her B.A. from Emory University and her J.D. from Florida State University, and worked as a lawyer before entering politics.

candidates.name: Juan Arauz
candidates.summary: Juan Arauz is a Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Kathy Castor in the Democratic primary for Florida's 14th Congressional District. He is running as a progressive alternative, with endorsements from groups such as the Progressive Voters Network. Arauz is on the ballot for the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Mike Beltran
candidates.summary: Mike Beltran is a Republican candidate for Florida's 14th Congressional District, a former state representative who served three terms in the Florida House from 2018 to 2024. A conservative Republican and attorney from Riverview, Beltran has self-funded $1 million into his campaign and emphasizes his anti-abortion, pro-Second Amendment record and independence from the Tallahassee establishment.

candidates.name: Kevin Steele
candidates.summary: Kevin Steele is a Republican candidate for Florida's 14th Congressional District and a current member of the Florida House of Representatives representing District 55 in Pasco County. A retired tech executive with a reported net worth exceeding $152 million, he previously self-funded $5 million into a campaign for Florida CFO before switching to this congressional race. Steele has highlighted his business background and his commitment to cutting taxes and reducing government spending.

candidates.name: John Peters
candidates.summary: John Peters is a Republican candidate for Florida's 14th Congressional District. He qualified for the ballot on June 8, 2026, and is running as a conservative businessman. Peters has been described as having shifted his candidacy from another district to challenge Kathy Castor following the 2026 redistricting.

candidates.name: Shay Williams
candidates.summary: Shay Williams is a Republican candidate for Florida's 14th Congressional District. He is a retired U.S. Coast Guard Commander and decorated military aviator who has also run for Florida House District 57. Williams emphasizes his military service and commitment to term limits and conservative principles.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists for this race, so the forecast rests entirely on structural and candidate factors. The May 2026 redistricting transformed this seat from Harris +7 (2024) to Trump +10 — a roughly 17-point Republican shift — giving the GOP a very strong underlying partisan baseline in the newly drawn district. Offsetting this, Democrat Kathy Castor is a 20-year incumbent (first elected 2006) with very high name recognition, established constituent ties, and a proven ability to outperform the district's partisan lean. The Republican primary (August 18) is crowded with four candidates including well-funded contenders Mike Beltran ($1M self-funded) and Kevin Steele (net worth $152M, self-funded $5M previously), adding uncertainty about nominee quality and post-primary party unity. Given the competing forces of a strongly Republican district versus a durable Democratic incumbent, and the complete absence of general-election polling data, the race is best characterized as a pure tossup with neither party showing a clear advantage at this pre-primary stage. Confidence is low due to zero polling availability and the fluid pre-primary environment.
